title: BIS Project Aurum Phase 2 Tests Privacy-Preserving Digital Cash
description: A BIS Innovation Hub prototype combines cryptographic privacy tools with configurable compliance controls for digital cash; it is a research proof of concept, not a live payment system.
why_it_matters: The prototype gives central banks a concrete architecture for testing whether digital cash can limit routine disclosure of payment data without removing compliance safeguards.
keyTakeaways: Project Aurum Phase 2 is an exploratory proof of concept rather than a production launch.
The prototype combines encryption, BBS+ signatures, pseudonymous ownership and zero-knowledge proofs.
BIS says stronger privacy can introduce trade-offs in performance, programmability and operational complexity.
body:
The BIS Innovation Hub published Project Aurum Phase 2 on October 13. The research prototype builds on Aurum's two-tier digital-cash architecture and adds privacy-enhancing technologies at the retail layer. It combines encryption, BBS+ signatures, pseudonym-based ownership and zero-knowledge proofs with configurable compliance mechanisms.

BIS presents the work as an exploratory proof of concept, not a deployed central bank digital currency or public payment service. The project examines a middle ground between complete anonymity and full transaction transparency. Its design separates responsibilities and data access while retaining payment-integrity controls.

The report also identifies trade-offs: stronger privacy may affect programmability, performance and operational complexity. The result is therefore a technical reference for further experimentation and policy discussion, not evidence that a central bank has approved or launched this architecture.

facts.claim: Project Aurum Phase 2 produced a research prototype rather than a live payment deployment.
The design uses BBS+ signatures as one of its privacy-enhancing technologies.
The prototype also uses zero-knowledge proofs.
Privacy features are implemented in the retail layer alongside compliance controls.
BIS published the Phase 2 report on October 13, 2026.
